subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up — Finex (tokens/sec, QPS, peak vs steady-state)
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (throughput & latency)

Hi Alex — great to meet you and Samantha on the call today. Thanks for walking us through Finex's streaming ingestion use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary:
- Workload: real-time ingestion + user-facing generation for alerts (low-latency)
- Current ask: understand throughput sizing (tokens/sec & QPS), concurrency and peak vs steady state, and streaming SLOs

Finex targets you called out:
- Latency target: 200ms median token latency for streaming responses (user-visible)
- Concurrent sessions: ~250 steady; spike up to ~1,200 for product launches
- Typical request size: 300-1,200 tokens (median ~520 tokens)
- QPS baseline: ~18 req/s (steady), peak bursts up to 85 req/s for ~10–20 minutes

Immediate next steps:
1) If you can share a quick sample of QPS by minute for a typical day and one peak day (CSV or exported metrics), we’ll run a sizing estimate against the models you mentioned.
2) Marissa (our infra lead) will follow up with specific questions on streaming behavior (prefix caching, KV reuse) and recommended concurrency model.
3) We’ll propose a sizing plan (GPU count + cluster config), and an estimated cost range, by EOD Monday.

Attachments: placeholder for sample CSV (finex-qps-sample.csv) — please attach when you reply.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finex.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (throughput & latency)

Thanks Rafael — recap looks good. I attached a small CSV with minute-level QPS for a recent week (finex-qps-sample.csv). A few clarifications: 

- The 200ms median is what product expects for the first 8 tokens of a streaming response (we can tolerate higher tail for long generations).
- For concurrent sessions: the 250 steady number is for our EU+US combined traffic; the spike 1,200 is mostly US-only during marketing events.
- We currently batch at the app level in bursts (~50ms windows) but would like to explore server-side batching from Redwood to reduce cost.

Let us know if the CSV is sufficient or you need different granularity. Happy to jump on a 30-min sizing call next week.

— Alex
Alex Johnson | Sr. PM, Finex
alex.johnson@finex.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finex.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (throughput & latency) — Marissa follow-up (technical)

Hi Alex — thanks for the CSV, I took a quick look. A few technical follow-ups so we can size more accurately: 

1) Tokenization: are your token counts in the CSV pre-tokenized? If not, what’s the average input token size per request?
2) Streaming: do you require server push (chunked streaming) for every token, or are you OK with partial buffering (e.g., emit every 50 tokens)?
3) KV reuse / conversation state: are requests independent or do they reuse a session-level KV cache per user (this affects memory/KV cache sizing heavily)?
4) SLA expectations: do you expect strict SLO enforcement (automatic failover to smaller models) during peaks, or would you prefer best-effort with alerts?

If convenient, can you answer 1–3 in a reply; Rafael and I will synthesize and send a recommended cluster configuration.

Warmly,
Marissa Cole | Infra Solutions Engineer
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (throughput & latency)

Thanks Marissa — answers below inline: 

1) Tokenization: the CSV shows request counts; we estimate average input tokens ~420 and output ~100 tokens per request (so ~520 tokens total median). We can get you pre-tokenized exports if helpful.
2) Streaming: we need true token-level streaming (UI shows tokens as they arrive). Emitting every 50 tokens is acceptable for lower-priority paths but primary alert flows need per-token low-latency streaming.
3) KV reuse: we maintain a short session KV (last ~1,000 tokens) per active user for context; sessions are pinned to users for ~12 hours.
4) SLA: product team wants automatic fallback (smaller model) during overload windows with notification; not strict financial penalties but high availability is required.

I attached the sample CSV as requested (finex-qps-sample.csv). Let me know if you need the pre-tokenized dataset.

— Alex
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Throughput sizing follow-up — prep notes for sizing call

Neha — forwarding the thread. Key numbers from Finex: median total tokens ~520, steady QPS ~18, peak bursts to ~85 QPS, steady concurrency ~250, spike concurrency ~1,200, token-level streaming required for primary flows, short session KV cached (~1,000 tokens). Attachments: finex-qps-sample.csv.

Can you pull together a 30-min runbook: 
- Quick cluster config options (3 flavors: cost-optimized, balanced, SLA-first) with estimated GPU counts and rough monthly cost ranges
- Notes on autoscale thresholds, caching parameters, and recommended fallback model mapping for failover during spikes

Target to have a draft by tomorrow noon PST so Rafael can share with Finex before the call. Thanks — Rafael
